html:
In 1923 Liechtenstein signed a customs union with Switzerland, turning away from Austria after the fall of the Habsburg empire.

Until the First World War the principality had shared customs and money with Austria. The war and Austria's inflation ruined it. It took the Swiss franc as its currency and linked its customs, post and borders to Switzerland, which still represents it in many countries.

With low taxes and easy company law from the 1920s, Liechtenstein grew from a poor farming land into one of the richest states per person in the world, with banks, trusts and industry such as dental products and tools. It joined the European Economic Area in 1995 but not the European Union. See also the princely house.
sum: In 1923 Liechtenstein signed a customs union with Switzerland, turning away from Austria after the fall of the Habsburg empire.
